Package com.nexuslink.protocol.secrets

Class VaultService

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.secrets.VaultService
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class VaultService extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A thin HashiCorp Vault client over the JDK HTTP client (no heavy HTTP dependency). Covers the pieces an engineer reaches for when testing a Vault: authenticating (direct token or AppRole), a health probe, and full KV v2 secret CRUD (read / write / list / delete).

The token is sent in the X-Vault-Token header; an optional Vault Enterprise namespace is sent in X-Vault-Namespace. All calls are blocking and are expected to run off the UI thread. Path building lives in VaultPaths so it can be unit-tested offline.

    • request

      public com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode request(String method, String apiPath, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode body)
      Issues an authenticated Vault API call and returns the parsed JSON body (an empty object for a 204/empty response). apiPath is relative to the server address, e.g. v1/sys/health. Used by the higher-level methods above and available for less-common endpoints (e.g. enabling an auth method in tests). Vault's LIST verb is sent as a GET with ?list=true since the JDK client rejects non-standard method names.
